sections.title: Why study Automobile Engineering in France?
sections.lead: \\Automobile Engineering PG in France\\ is a good option for students who want to develop specialized knowledge in automobile technology and vehicle development.

groups.text: \\Benefits of studying automobile engineering in France are:\\

items: \\Specialisms in Electric and Hybrid Vehicles:\\ Specialize in electric vehicles, hybrid propulsion, battery technology and sustainable mobility.
\\Advanced Automotive Training:\\ Learn vehicle dynamics, engine systems, control engineering and automotive electronics.
\\Research Opportunities:\\ Learn research and product-development skills via academic projects and lab work.
\\Industry Exposure:\\ Opportunities to learn in engineering schools and automotive research labs.
\\Specialised Career Pathways:\\ Discover career opportunities in automotive manufacturing, electric mobility, motorsport and vehicle technology.
\\International Learning Environment:\\ Specific programs are offered in English and French based on the school.

sections.title: Mechanical Engineering Courses in France
sections.lead: \\Postgraduate Automobile Engineering courses in France\\ can be national master degrees, specialized engineering programs or advanced professional qualifications. The right course depends on whether students want to focus on vehicle design, mechanical systems, electronics or sustainable transportation.

items: \\Popular Automobile Engineering specializations in France\\ are:
Automotive Engineering: Vehicle architecture, automotive systems, performance, product development.
Electric & Hybrid Vehicles: Electric powertrains, batteries, energy management, propulsion control.
Vehicle Dynamics: Modeling and Simulation of Vehicle Handling, Stability, Suspension Systems.
Automotive Design and Manufacturing: Computer-aided design, materials, manufacturing processes and vehicle development.
Automotive Electronics & Embedded Systems Electronic control units, sensors, software, diagnostics, vehicle communication.
Sustainable Mobility: alternative fuels, energy efficiency, fleet management and responsible transport.
Motorsport Engineering: Car performance, racing systems, aerodynamics, data analysis.

One relevant option that is taught in English is the \\Master in Automotive Engineering for Sustainable Mobility (AESM)\\, a joint program of Polytech Orléans and ISAT. It is a two year program with two specializations: Energy Management and Control for Sustainable Mobility or Vehicle Dynamics and Intelligent Vehicles for Sustainable Mobility.

sections.title: Eligibility Requirements
sections.lead: \\Automobile Engineering PG eligibility in France\\ differs for each institution and qualification. Applicants usually need an undergraduate degree in engineering or applied science.

items: Usually acceptable academic backgrounds are:
Automotive or Automobile Engineering
Mechanical Engineering (ME)
Mechatronics Engineering
Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Instrumentation & Control Engineering
Aeronautical Engineering
Other related disciplines in Engineering or Applied Science (where acceptable)
Students applying directly to a second-year master's program or a specialized post-master course may require a more advanced qualification or relevant professional experience.
Indian students should check the accepted undergraduate qualifications and subject prerequisites before applying for \\Automobile Engineering postgraduate courses in France.\\

sections.title: French PG Automobile Engineering Admission Requirements
sections.lead: Prospective students should check the official requirements of their preferred university. \\Eligibility criteria for Automobile Engineering in France\\ usually include:

items: \\Academic Qualifications:\\ A recognized bachelor's degree or equivalent in an appropriate engineering or scientific subject.

\\English Language Proficiency:\\ IELTS, TOEFL, TOEIC, Cambridge qualifications or other evidence as required for English language taught programs. The minimum score requirements for the AESM program are IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 80, TOEFL 550, or TOEIC 785. Candidates should check current requirements with the admissions team.
\\Knowledge of French:\\ Some English taught programs do not require French but it can be a great asset for those seeking internships and jobs in France.
\\Academic Qualifications:\\ A good academic record in subjects such as mechanics, mathematics, thermodynamics, electronics and control systems may support an application.

\\Additional selection criteria:\\ Universities may ask for additional documents depending on the program – this could be a motivation letter, letters of recommendation, a CV, an interview or proof of relevant projects and internships.
Applicants should also check if a program requires certified translations, specific document formats or a separate application process for international students.

sections.title: Tuition Fees for Automobile Engineering in France
sections.lead: \\The cost of studying Automobile Engineering in France\\ depends on the institution, program, student status, and city.

items: For the academic year 2026-2027, Campus France provides the following reference tuition rates for public higher education institutions subject to the national fee system:
National Master's degree \| €255/year \| €3,950/year

The €3,950 non-EU master's rate and the €630 engineering-degree rate do not apply to each other. The amount varies by the institution and qualification. \Exemptions and institution specific fees may apply.
For instance, the Université d'Orléans mentions a \\€5,750 per year for the AESM programme\. Students are requested to contact the institution for updated tuition fees.
Additional Cost of Living in France
In addition to \\Automobile Engineering tuition fees in France\\, students also need to budget for:
Lodging and utilities.
Daily expenses and food.
Local transport.
Costs related to health and insurance, if applicable.
Books, software and study materials.
Visa and travel and personal costs.
The cost of living depends on the city and type of accommodation. Students are advised to calculate the full cost of study before accepting an offer of admission.
## 7. Admission Process for Automobile Engineering PG in France
\\Steps involved in the admission process for Automobile Engineering PG in France\\:
1. \\Shortlist Programmes:\\ Compare specialization, language of instruction, duration, location and qualification type.
2. \\Check Academic Requirements:\\ Check the requirements for degree, subject, and academic performance.
3. \\Prepare Documents Collect transcripts, degree certificates, CV, motivation letter, recommendations and language-test results (if needed).
4. \\Apply through the Correct Channel:\\ Apply through the university's official portal or the application process for international students.
5. \\Final Selection Stages:\\ Interviews or further academic information may be requested.
6. \\Receive your Admission Decision:\\ Review the offer of admission, tuition fees, deadlines and conditions for enrollment.
7. \\Finalize your financial and immigration requirements:\\ Follow the student visa process for your situation and prepare the necessary financial documentation.
8. \\Complete Registration\\: Submit any outstanding documents and follow the institution's registration procedures.

The official university page for the AESM program indicates that the \\2027–2028 recruitment campaign\\ will commence on 1 November 2026 and conclude on 31 May 2027. Candidates are advised to visit the official page for updates before applying.

sections.title: Recognition and Accreditation of Automobile Engineering Degrees in France
sections.lead: When enrolling for a \\Automobile Engineering postgraduate program in France\\students should not just look at the program title but also check the qualification awarded by the institution.

items: The main types of qualifications to know are:
\\Master's Degree:\\ A master's degree recognized at the national level within the French higher education system.
\\Engineering diploma\\: obtained from an authorized engineering school. Recognition and status depends on the particular diploma.
\\Postgraduate Specialisation:\\ A professional or specialist course that does not correspond to a national master's degree.
The AESM program is listed by Université d'Orléans as a co-accredited Master's level program with ISAT, registered at level BAC+5.
Before you apply, students should check:
the official title of the degree and the institution that granted it.
whether the program leads to a national master's degree, an engineering diploma or a specialization.
The institution's accreditation or recognition status.
duration and academic credits.
requirements for recognition of employment or further study in the destination country.

sections.title: Salary and Job Opportunities After Automobile Engineering PG in France
sections.lead: A \\Master's in Automobile Engineering in France\\ opens up the door to job prospects in vehicle development, automotive systems, electric mobility, manufacturing, testing and research.

items: The employment outcomes are dependent on the specialization, practical experience, language skills, location and labor market conditions.
Possible \\jobs after Automobile Engineering PG in France\\ are:
Automotive Design Engineer
Vehicle Dynamics Engineer
Electric Vehicle Systems Engineer
Powertrain Engineer
Automotive Simulation Engineer
Automotive Electronics or Embedded-Systems Engineer
Testing and Validation Engineer
Automotive Manufacturing Engineer
Motorsport Engineer
Research and Development Engineer
Sustainable Mobility Engineer

Potential employers include car manufacturers, suppliers of vehicle components, electric mobility companies, engineering consultancies, testing organizations, motorsport companies and research laboratories.
Automobile Engineering Salary in France
There is no one salary for all automobile engineering graduates. Pay varies according to experience, duties, employer, location and technical specialization.

French language skills are useful for local employment, teamwork and communication with manufacturers and suppliers. Graduates who wish to pursue research, either in academia or in industry, may also do a PhD if they meet the relevant entry requirements.

sections.title: Documents Needed for Automobile Engineering PG in France
sections.lead: The checklist is specific to institutions. Documents generally asked for admission in Automobile Engineering in France are:

items: Accepted identity document or valid passport.
Bachelor's Degree Certificate / Provisional Certificate.
Academic transcripts and marksheets.
Resume or CV.
Motivation letter or statement of purpose.
Test results in English or French as appropriate.
Letters of recommendation, if desired.
Course descriptions or syllabus of prior study where applicable.
Certificates of internship or employment (if applicable).
Technical project or research details if asked.
Certified translations of documents if required.
Application form completed.
Receipt of application fee, if any.

With the AESM application form you need to submit a CV, a copy of your passport, a motivation letter, the curriculum of your undergraduate course, your degree certificates, your transcripts, two reference letters and your English-language test results.
The checklist for the academic application is different from the visa and enrollment documents. Upon receiving an admission decision, students must adhere to the official instructions provided.

faqs.q: \\ Can international students pursue Automobile Engineering in France?
faqs.a: Yes. International students (including Indian students) can apply for eligible automotive engineering masters and specialist programs if they meet the academic, language and application requirements.

faqs.q: FAQ What French universities provide post-graduate automotive engineering?
faqs.a: For the \\Automotive Engineering for Sustainable Mobility master's programme\\students may also consider ISAT and Polytech Orléans, in addition to ESTACA and ISAE-Supméca for suitable automotive or mechanical engineering tracks.

faqs.q: Do you have postgraduate courses in automobile engineering in English?
faqs.a: Yep. The AESM program is a joint program offered by Polytech Orléans and ISAT in English language. Some other programs may be taught in French or a combination of languages, so students should check the language for the intake that they are interested in.

faqs.q: What is the fee structure for Automobile Engineering PG in France?
faqs.a: Tuition fees depend on the qualification and institution. For the academic year 2026-2027 the national reference fee for a subsidized Master's degree course is €3,950 per year for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. The Université d'Orléans has AESM at 5,750 €/year. Students are responsible to check with the institutions concerned.

faqs.q: What are the job opportunities after PG in Automobile Engineering in France?
faqs.a: Graduate career options include vehicle design, electric vehicle systems, powertrain development, testing, simulation, manufacturing, motorsport and automotive research. The opportunities you will have in your career depend on your experience, your specialization, the languages you speak, and the requirements of the employer.
